recent_from_earlier.reader_point: Read about how the EU is sanctioning the individuals, companies, organisations and disinformation actors complicit in Russia's war with Ukraine.
recent_from_earlier.why_it_matters: Entity-level financial and business restrictions are a direct EU instrument for limiting foreign war-related capital and technology access.
recent_from_earlier.matrix_basis: Source evidence: For Horizon Europe (except the European Research Council and the European Innovation Council), all legal entities (public and private) established in Russia, Belarus or in non-government controlled territories of Ukraine are not eligible to participate.
recent_from_earlier.metadata_correction_reason: The source’s explicit most recent page-update date is 12 October 2026. Original 2020-01-01 scanner date predates 2022 invasion and cannot describe this work.
recent_from_earlier.reader_title: EU targeted sanctions on individuals and organisations
recent_from_earlier.reader_what: The Commission documents EU asset freezes, travel restrictions and bans affecting people and organisations connected to Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.
recent_from_earlier.reader_why: Entity-level financial and business restrictions are a direct EU instrument for limiting foreign war-related capital and technology access.
recent_from_earlier.reader_more: The official Commission overview summarizes restrictive measures, affected sectors, sanctions-circumvention support, state financing and bans on propaganda-channel distribution. It is a changing reference webpage updated in October 2026, not an original 2020 issuance or a fixed 2020 legal package. The page records the Commission’s implementation account and categories, not independent evidence of sanctions effectiveness.

deep_analysis.research_question: What entity-level economic and financial measures form part of the EU response to Russia’s war in Ukraine?
deep_analysis.main_finding: The EU has implemented asset freezes and restrictive measures applying to individuals and organisations in Russia and certain third-country circumvention networks.
deep_analysis.method_or_basis: Full matching Commission sanctions information page, last updated 12 October 2026, cross-checkable against the EU sanctions acts.
deep_analysis.qualification: Sanction counts change over time and are official Commission figures; the webpage cannot be retrospectively dated to 2020.
deep_analysis.radar_relevance: Direct EU external financial coercion, sanctions circumvention and cross-border entity controls.

earlier_from_recent.title: Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on the European Union Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA), the European cybersecurity certification framework, and ICT supply chain security and repealing Regulation (EU) 2019/881 (The Cybersecurity Act 2) - Publications Office of the EU
earlier_from_recent.summary: The Commission's 2026 proposal and EU institutional procedure record specify ICT supply-chain provisions and an ongoing legislative process. It is a proposal under EU legislative consideration, not an enacted regulation or automatic vendor exclusion.
earlier_from_recent.core_message: The draft Cybersecurity Act 2 would revise ENISA's role, cybersecurity certification and ICT supplier risk management.
earlier_from_recent.relevance_note: A: detailed EU strategic technology and critical-infrastructure supplier screening instrument.
earlier_from_recent.metadata_correction_reason: The matched EU law proposal was issued as COM(2026) 11 on 20 January 2026; the scanner used the October Publications Office URL date.

earlier_from_recent.reader_what: The draft Cybersecurity Act 2 would revise ENISA's role, cybersecurity certification and ICT supplier risk management.
